newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia's wildlife at risk from pollution, farming.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's wildlife at risk from pollution, farming.

text.p: The Mediterranean sea lion, which became the mascot of the 1979 Mediterranean Games in Split, can no longer be found in Croatian waters and many other species look set to die out, officials said on Friday.
The sea lion was one of a number of endangered plants and animals that is growing because of pollution and poor farming and forestry projects which do not protect natural habitats.
Croatia signed a convention on biological diversity in January 1997 which calls for all European signatories to submit a list of endangered species.

Jasminka Radovic, who works at an organisation responsible for protecting Croatia's cultural and natural heritage, said the new list would contain more species than the previous one, written in 1994, though the full total is not yet known.

"The last red alert list...contained some 41 endangered animals and 226 plants, while now we are are trying to assess the actual number of plant and animal species living in the region. This will help us determine the current situation," Radovic said.
But the situation isn't all bad, she added. Wolves and bears are thriving in Croatia.
